chunks: And in the narration of Aban, he said:

"Al-ja'ifah is that which enters the inner cavity; there is no qisas for its victim, only hukumah. Al-munaqqilah, from which the bones are displaced, there is no qisas in it, only hukumah. And in al-ma'mumah there is one-third of the diyah; there is no qisas in it, only hukumah."

key_terms.اَلْجَائِفَةُ: A wound that penetrates into the body cavity.
key_terms.اَلْحُكُومَةُ: A compensatory judicial assessment for an injury.
key_terms.اَلْمَأْمُومَةِ: A head wound reaching the membrane surrounding the brain.
key_terms.اَلْمُنَقِّلَةُ: A wound in which bones are displaced.
key_terms.ثُلُثُ اَلدِّيَةِ: One-third of the prescribed blood money.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on qisas and diyah for al-ja'ifah, al-munaqqilah, and al-ma'mumah wounds?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for certain serious wounds in Islamic law. It states that for al-ja'ifah and al-munaqqilah there is no qisas, and only hukumah applies, while for al-ma'mumah one-third of the diyah is due, and qisas is likewise not applied.
